items.headline: Cursor links trojanized Claude Code extension on its marketplace to key stolen in Fireworks AI breach
items.summary: Cursor says an attacker used an access key issued to Fireworks AI, which was exposed in a breach at Fireworks. The incident ended with a trojanized version of the Claude Code extension on Cursor's extension marketplace. The full scope and number of affected users are not clear from the source.
items.importance_rationale: A popular developer extension was compromised and distributed through a marketplace, which is a supply-chain compromise involving the Claude Code watch technology.
items.detection_coverage_note: Our assessment is that monitoring which IDE extensions are installed and where developer endpoints connect would help, but the source gives no indicators.
items.recommended_action: List the Cursor and Claude Code extensions installed across your developer machines, then compare them with vendor guidance. Rotate any credentials exposed on endpoints that ran a suspect version.
overrides: Global deployment applicability: every region 85%; cross-industry relevance at least 50%
items.model_importance_rationale: A popular developer extension was compromised and distributed through a marketplace, which is a supply-chain compromise involving the Claude Code watch technology.

items.headline: Cursor confirms breach enabled distribution of malicious Claude Code extension via its marketplace
items.summary: Cursor confirmed a security breach in which attackers distributed a malicious Claude Code extension through its extension marketplace. According to the report, the attackers got in using credentials stolen from AI infrastructure provider Fireworks AI. The source does not say how many users installed the extension or what it did.
items.importance_rationale: A popular developer-tool marketplace was compromised to push a malicious extension. This counts as a supply-chain compromise affecting developers worldwide.
items.detection_coverage_note: No detection rules were provided. Our assessment: check developer endpoints for unexpected extension installs and unusual outbound connections or credential access from IDE processes.
items.recommended_action: List the Cursor and Claude Code extensions installed across your organisation and remove any that look suspicious. Rotate secrets that are reachable from affected developer machines. Watch for vendor IOCs, since the full scope is still unclear.
overrides: Global deployment applicability: every region 85%; cross-industry relevance at least 50%
items.model_importance_rationale: A popular developer-tool marketplace was compromised to push a malicious extension. This counts as a supply-chain compromise affecting developers worldwide.

items.headline: US disrupts North Korean 'FaceStealer' social engineering campaign tied to $400M crypto theft
items.summary: The US government says it has disrupted 'FaceStealer', a North Korean social engineering campaign blamed for stealing more than $400 million in cryptocurrency. The source does not detail the specific techniques used or who the victims were.
items.importance_rationale: A major government disruption of a large-scale nation-state theft campaign.
items.detection_coverage_note: The source provides no technical indicators. Assessment: rely on social engineering awareness and controls on high-risk staff.
items.recommended_action: Watch for published indicators of compromise. Brief staff who handle crypto or finance on North Korean social engineering lures.
items.model_importance_rationale: A major government disruption of a large-scale nation-state theft campaign.

items.headline: CISA adds actively exploited UnrealIRCd command injection flaw CVE-2026-114713 to KEV
items.summary: CISA has added CVE-2026-114713 (CVSS 8.6) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after reports that attackers are exploiting it. The flaw affects UnrealIRCd, an open-source IRC server, and comes from improper neutralization of delimiters, which allows command injection at the server level. UnrealIRCd is a niche product in enterprise environments.
items.importance_rationale: The flaw is in CISA KEV and is being actively exploited. UnrealIRCd is not widely deployed enterprise software, so this rates high rather than critical.
items.detection_coverage_note: The source links no detection rules. Assessment: watch IRC server hosts for unexpected child processes and outbound connections.
items.recommended_action: Check whether any UnrealIRCd instances are running, including shadow IT. Patch them per vendor guidance and review the hosts for signs of compromise.
items.model_importance_rationale: The flaw is in CISA KEV and is being actively exploited. UnrealIRCd is not widely deployed enterprise software, so this rates high rather than critical.

Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.

items.headline: Grafana Recorded Queries flaw (CVE-2026-12933) lets editors send requests to data source hosts
items.summary: CVE-2026-12933 is a flaw in Grafana. Its Recorded Queries remote-write endpoint tests connections with elevated credentials before checking whether the caller has permission. An attacker with organization editor rights could send authenticated requests to a data source host and infer sensitive data from the replies.
items.importance_rationale: The flaw requires authentication and has no reported exploitation or PoC.
items.detection_coverage_note: Our assessment is that you should review Grafana audit logs for unexpected creation of Recorded Queries remote-write targets.
items.recommended_action: Look up which Grafana versions are affected in vendor advisories, as the Amazon Linux record does not confirm affected status or patches. Patch when fixes are available, and limit who holds editor roles.
items.model_importance_rationale: The flaw requires authentication and has no reported exploitation or PoC.

items.headline: Italian regulator fines Meta €805 million over Facebook Android gallery access
items.summary: Italy's data protection authority (Garante/GPDP) fined Meta €805 million. It found that a Facebook for Android feature accessed users' photos and videos without valid consent.
items.importance_rationale: This is a large GDPR enforcement action, but the company fined is not in a target industry. It is useful as a privacy-consent precedent.
items.detection_coverage_note: This is a regulatory action, so detection does not apply.
items.recommended_action: Check that mobile app features which access personal data are turned off by default and only run after explicit consent.
items.model_importance_rationale: This is a large GDPR enforcement action, but the company fined is not in a target industry. It is useful as a privacy-consent precedent.

items.headline: Italy's Garante fines Meta €805M for default-on Facebook Android gallery access without consent
items.summary: The Garante found that a Facebook for Android photo-suggestion feature was switched on by default. It says the feature accessed Italian users' photos, videos and metadata without explicit consent. Meta reportedly has 60 days to respond or comply.
items.importance_rationale: This is a large GDPR fine against a company outside the target industries.
items.detection_coverage_note: This is a regulatory action, so detection does not apply.
items.recommended_action: Check consent defaults in mobile apps that access device media.
items.model_importance_rationale: This is a large GDPR fine against a company outside the target industries.

items.headline: GNU cpio through 2.15 has an out-of-bounds read when parsing newc/crc archive headers
items.summary: GNU cpio through version 2.15 has an out-of-bounds stack read in from_ascii() when it parses newc and crc archive headers. If the checksum field contains only spaces, the parser reads past the header buffer and may decode nearby stack bytes as header values. The Amazon Linux record does not say whether Amazon Linux is affected or whether a patch is available, and no exploitation is reported.
items.importance_rationale: The flaw is a memory-safety bug in a common Linux utility, but it is an out-of-bounds read with limited impact. The source gives no CVSS score, proof of concept or reported exploitation.
items.detection_coverage_note: The source has no detection rules. Network or SIEM detection is likely to have limited value here, so finding vulnerable versions through package inventory is the practical control.
items.recommended_action: Find systems running GNU cpio 2.15 or earlier and track distribution advisories for fixed packages, since patch status is not yet confirmed. Until then, avoid processing untrusted cpio archives in automated pipelines.
items.model_importance_rationale: The flaw is a memory-safety bug in a common Linux utility, but it is an out-of-bounds read with limited impact. The source gives no CVSS score, proof of concept or reported exploitation.

items.headline: Italian authority fines Meta $887 million over Facebook access to Android gallery content
items.summary: An Italian authority fined Meta about $887 million over Facebook's access to photos and videos in Android device galleries. The authority said the relevant directive treats smartphones as part of a person's private sphere and requires free and informed consent for such access.
items.importance_rationale: This is a large privacy enforcement action in Europe, but it targets a consumer platform rather than a target industry.
items.recommended_action: Review how your mobile apps ask for consent before accessing device data in the EU.
items.model_importance_rationale: This is a large privacy enforcement action in Europe, but it targets a consumer platform rather than a target industry.

items.headline: Malvertising on Dutch news sites tried to infect iPhones with malware
items.summary: Attackers used the ad system on several Dutch websites, including VI, Autoblog and GeenStijl, to serve code that tried to infect iPhones with malware. The source does not say whether any devices were successfully compromised.
items.importance_rationale: A regional malvertising campaign against consumer iPhones. There is no evidence of enterprise impact or confirmed compromise.
items.detection_coverage_note: No detection rules were provided. Our assessment: mobile threat defence and DNS filtering logs may show visits to the malicious ad domains.
items.recommended_action: Make sure managed iPhones are running the latest iOS version. Keep watching for IOCs, because whether any infections succeeded is still unconfirmed.
items.model_importance_rationale: A regional malvertising campaign against consumer iPhones. There is no evidence of enterprise impact or confirmed compromise.

items.headline: ESLint ends paid contributor program as AI-generated code strains open-source maintainers
items.summary: ESLint has ended its paid contributor program. Several open-source projects, including Rust, Godot and curl, are tightening contribution rules because AI-generated submissions are putting pressure on maintainers.
items.importance_rationale: This is ecosystem and governance news with no direct security incident.
items.recommended_action: Monitor the health of open-source projects you depend on as part of software composition analysis governance.
items.model_importance_rationale: This is ecosystem and governance news with no direct security incident.

items.headline: Opinion: Overreliance on AI may erode security teams' critical skills
items.summary: This SecurityWeek opinion piece argues that leaning too heavily on AI could weaken the creativity, communication and critical thinking that security teams need when no playbook applies. It reports no incident or vulnerability.
items.recommended_action: No action required. Optionally include skills retention in your AI usage policy.

items.headline: datasette-llm 0.1a11 adds support for OpenAI-compatible endpoints and local models
items.summary: The datasette-llm plugin release 0.1a11 can now connect to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. This lets Datasette Agent run with local models through tools such as LM Studio, Ollama or llama.cpp.
items.importance_rationale: This is a minor open-source feature release with no security impact.
items.model_importance_rationale: This is a minor open-source feature release with no security impact.

items.headline: Schneier lists upcoming November 2026 speaking engagements in Canada
items.summary: Bruce Schneier lists two upcoming talks, both in Ontario, Canada, on November 18 and 19, 2026. The post contains no security news.
